content:
OpenAI is restructuring its organization to place voice at the center of its AI strategy. By merging its engineering, product, and research teams, the company is completely overhauling its voice models. The primary goal of this operational change is to develop a voice-focused personal hardware device scheduled for release in about a year.

Screen-Independent Interaction and the Jony Ive Effect

The new architecture being developed aims not only to enhance ChatGPT’s voice capabilities but also to create a hardware ecosystem that minimizes screen usage. Jony Ive, who is involved in the design process, is crafting a user experience that reduces device dependency and minimizes the demand for attention. The company’s long-term plans include screenless speakers or glasses-like wearable technologies.

The technical capabilities of the new voice model under development are as follows:

  • More natural intonation and emphasis.
  • Adapting to interruptions during speech.
  • The ability to respond in real time while the user continues speaking.
  • A real-time conversation experience with low latency.

Industry Competition and Market Conditions

Voice-focused interfaces have become a key focus for tech giants. While Meta is testing multi-microphone systems with its Ray-Ban smart glasses, Google is working on “Audio Overviews,” which convert search results into audio summaries. Tesla, meanwhile, aims to transform navigation management into natural conversations by integrating xAI’s Grok model into its in-vehicle systems. Having learned from previous failed hardware attempts, such as the Humane AI Pin, OpenAI aims to deliver a more robust and technically mature product by 2026.
